_readme: THE THREE PACK PLANS, AS STRIPE OBJECTS. Fresh objects — nothing here reuses or edits Chris Mejia's
'Yourgi Membership' feasibility test (prod_V19cNesnBYgwPl), which is a different offer and not ours.
This file is the single source of truth for what gets created in Stripe, and it is machine-checked
against the landing page: test/prototype.test.mjs asserts that every tier key, price and label here
matches the data-tier / data-price / data-label attributes in index.html. That check exists because
a mismatch between this file and the page is not a cosmetic bug — it bills someone the wrong price.
Change a price on the page and this file fails until you change it here too, and vice versa.
Amounts are in CENTS, as Stripe expects. $49.00 is 4900.
STATUS: prices are NOT approved (David owns them, blocking decision #1). Create these in a SANDBOX.
Every object carries status metadata saying so, so nobody finds them later and assumes otherwise.

payment_link._phone: Phone is OPTIONAL on the landing page, so this is where concierge actually gets a number. The page promises a callback within one business day; without this, some paying subscribers arrive unreachable.
payment_link._billing_address: auto, not required. The page's stated principle is that every required field before payment costs signups — that's why phone was made optional there. Chris's link used 'required'; if Finance needs it for tax, change it here and say why.
payment_link._redirect: Substitute the real page URL. The final slug is blocking decision #10, so this defaults to the GitHub Pages review URL — correct for sandbox testing, and one field to change later.
payment_link._consent: The page's beta band promises 'Cancel any month, and we'll tell you before your next charge if anything changes.' A recurring charge should say so before the card is entered, not only in the receipt. Wind-down terms are blocking decision #4 — if Legal narrows that promise, this text and the beta band both change together.
payment_link._submit_message: Each plan also sets custom_text.submit.message — the line directly above the Subscribe button — because it names the actual amount and so has to differ per plan. It lives on each plan below, not here. The earlier internal link used one too; it is the last thing a buyer reads before committing, so the number in it must be that plan's own price.

terms_of_service_acceptance.message: This is a monthly plan. It renews automatically and charges this card every month until you cancel. Cancel any month from the link on your receipt; cancellation takes effect at the end of the month you've paid for. Yourgi Plus is a limited beta — we'll tell you before your next charge if anything changes.

_subsidy_note: THIS IS THE UNCAPPED PLAN, and §6's subsidy guardrail is currently missing on it — a month of
nightly house-sitting for $499 with Pros paid full rate is the exposure §6 names by name.
index.html's head comment already flags it as needing a real answer before this page takes money.
There is a concrete guardrail available in Stripe itself, and Chris's link already used it:
restrictions.completed_sessions.limit caps how many people can ever complete checkout on a link.
Setting it turns 'unbounded exposure' into 'exposure bounded by N subscribers' — which is a real
answer to §6 rather than a copy change, and it's reversible by raising the number.
Left unset here on purpose: N is a business decision, not mine. Set it before live mode.
